name: KSH International Ltd
tagline: Debt-free magnet-winding-wire maker (India's #3, #1 exporter) riding a T&D/HVDC and electrification tailwind - FY26 revenue +61%, Q1 FY27 revenue ~doubled, specialised/CTC wire +113% YoY, EBITDA/ton surging, and a new 5-year Hitachi Energy supply framework - but only listed Dec 2025 and trading at ~57x P/E near its 52-week high
business_overview: KSH International (est. 1979/1981) is India's leading manufacturer of bare and insulated rectangular and round magnet winding wires and transposed cables, serving OEMs across power/distribution transformers, railways, automotive, renewables, and industrial motor/generator applications from three plants near Mumbai and Pune.
fundamentals_table: Revenue Rs 3,107 Cr (+61%); PAT Rs 110.1 Cr (+62%); EBITDA/ton Rs 67,625 (from Rs 52,536 FY25)

Revenue Rs 1,164 Cr (~+100% YoY); PAT Rs 42.2 Cr (+86%); EBITDA Rs 74.4 Cr (+85%, 6.39% margin); volume 7,999 MT (from 6,100); EBITDA/ton Rs 93,000 (TTM ~Rs 74,000); specialised wire +113% YoY; exports +76% YoY
43,445 MT (Mar 2026, incl 14,400 MT Supa Phase I commissioned Sep 2025); plan 59,045 MT by end-FY27
fundamentals_narrative: Every quality dimension the thesis screens for is genuinely strong: ROCE ~21%, ROE ~20%, debt-free, and a 5-year revenue/profit CAGR of ~47%/~50%. The FY26 and Q1 FY27 prints show a live acceleration, not just a trailing average - FY26 revenue +61%, Q1 FY27 revenue ~doubled to Rs 1,164 Cr, PAT +86%, volume 7,999 MT (from 6,100), and EBITDA/ton jumped to Rs 93,000 against a TTM ~Rs 74,000 as the mix shifted to specialised and CTC (continuously transposed conductor) wire (75% of revenue, +113% YoY) and exports (+76% YoY). Management signed a five-year supply framework agreement with Hitachi Energy Global and is lifting capacity from 43,445 MT to 59,045 MT by end-FY27. The caveats are valuation and history: the stock listed only in December 2025, so this record predates sustained public scrutiny, it trades at ~57x P/E near its 52-week high, and the base business is a thin-margin (~6% EBITDA) copper-spread converter, so EBITDA/ton can normalise. A promoter affiliate (KSH Distriparks) applied in September 2026 for reclassification from Promoter Group to Public - a logistics entity, not the operating promoters exiting.
technical_read: Current price (~Rs 1,005) sits just below the 52-week high (Rs 1,060), having risen sharply from the 52-week low (Rs 330) -- a name that has already re-rated significantly since listing.

verdict_reasoning: Quality gate is cleanly cleared: ROCE ~21%, ROE ~20%, debt-free, 5-yr revenue/profit CAGR ~47%/~50%, and the trailing record is NOT stale - FY26 revenue +61%, Q1 FY27 revenue ~doubled, PAT +86%, EBITDA/ton up to Rs 93,000 from Rs 52,536 in FY25 on a structural specialised/CTC/export mix shift.

four_box scores 2.0 (tailwind yes; tam weak - thin-margin copper-spread niche; moat weak - specialised capability, not pricing power; valuation no - ~57x P/E near the 52-week high, <1 year of public history). Per the decision table, 2.0 permits the return-magnitude label ONLY via a written exception: phreak's un-ignorable-growth carve-out applies here (revenue doubling, specialised wire +113% YoY, EBITDA/ton surging, Hitachi Energy 5-yr framework). Label allowed; conviction caps at Medium and is set to Low-Medium with an explicit 'unconfirmed' caveat.

Conviction not higher: ~57x P/E leaves no margin of safety, the business is a ~6%-EBITDA converter whose EBITDA/ton can normalise (peak_margin_risk flagged), there is no ValuePickr company thread for independent diligence, and public history is under a year. The only signal is joinjp2003's (trusted, elevated) repeat portfolio-thread mention - trusted_floor is false, so no conviction floor.

Red-flag check: none. Debt-free, no pledge, no auditor issue, no SEBI action. The KSH Distriparks promoter->public reclassification is a logistics affiliate, not an operating-promoter exit - not a HIGH CAUTION trigger.
Re-check after Q2/Q3 FY27: does EBITDA/ton hold near Rs 90k, does Supa Phase II commission and fill, and how firm is the Hitachi framework in actual offtake.

four_box.note: Tailwind yes: T&D/HVDC grid capex + EV traction + railways; the Hitachi Energy 5-yr supply framework validates it. TAM weak: India's #3 magnet-wire maker in a thin-margin (~6% EBITDA) copper-spread niche - real headroom via specialised/CTC mix + capacity doubling but the profit pool is capped. Moat weak: specialised CTC capability + export qualification, not structural pricing power. Valuation no: P/E ~57x near the 52-week high, <1 year of public history. Score 2.0 - the 10x-in-2-3-years label rests on phreak's un-ignorable-growth carve-out (see verdict_reasoning); conviction capped at Low-Medium, unconfirmed.
